title: Geography, B.S. (College of Earth and Mineral Sciences)
notes: Confirmed via a programmatic diff of the archived 2024-2025 bulletin edition against the current live 2026-27 edition and against each other archived edition (2022-23 through 2025-26): the 'Suggested Academic Plan' (semester-by-semester table) and 'Program Requirements' course lists for Geography, B.S. at University Park are byte-identical across all five editions -- same total credits (120), same required GEOG course numbers (210, 220, 230, 260, 301, 364, 390, 361/362/363/365 x2, 464, 493/494/495/499 engaged scholarship), same '300-level Geography (select 9 credits)'/'400-level Geography (select 12 credits)' categories, and the same STAT 200 prerequisite chain (the archived 2024-2025 STAT course-description page confirms STAT 200's 'Prerequisite at Enrollment: Placement into MATH 21 or higher' was already in place in 2024-2025, not a recent change -- so the STAT 100 fallback modeled below is not 2026-specific, it applies to this catalog year too). The only real differences found across editions are cosmetic course-title relabelings that don't change any course code this plan schedules (e.g. GEOG 363 'Image Analysis' -> 'Remote Sensing and Image Analysis' between 2023-24 and 2024-25; GEOG 210 'Perspectives on Human Geography' -> 'People, Place, and Power' -> 'Are we geographic?' across later editions; similar wording-only retitles for GEOG 220, 230, and several open-elective-pool 300/400-level topics course titles) and elective-pool course additions/removals in the department's own broader course list, which this plan already models generically via open_elective slots rather than an enumerated list, so those additions/removals don't affect this file. University Park. Every core GEOG course has zero listed prerequisites, so ordering follows the bulletin's own suggested sequence directly. 'Supporting Course' pool (bulletin: 'in geography or related areas') is modeled generically. Real prereq-fix fallout: STAT 200 (Semester 2) requires MATH 21, which itself requires MATH 4 and MATH 3 -- a full remedial placement chain never otherwise scheduled in this plan. No GEOG course actually enforces a STAT 200 prereq in the catalog, so rather than adding three remedial math courses, added STAT 100 (Statistical Concepts and Reasoning, no prereq, same STAT department) as a fallback option; the item now resolves to STAT 100 (3cr instead of 4cr). The '300-level Geography (select 9 credits)' and '400-level Geography (select 12 credits)' categories are wired via open_elective with elective_min_level/elective_max_level (300-399 and 400-499 respectively) and every other loaded department excluded via elective_exclude_prefixes, matching the same fix applied to the 2026 plan, since the archived 2024-2025 page has the identical bare, unrestricted category wording. The final 'Elective' slots (bulletin: 9 general-elective credits, not geography-specific) are left as bare placeholders since nothing restricts them to any particular department, same as the 2026 plan.
